name: Build macOS Release (Fa)

# Issue #343: the daily-publish CLI leg and a human can dispatch this
# workflow in the same window; the run-name embeds the input so the
# watcher's displayTitle match (the only distinguisher in the run-list
# API) never adopts someone else's run.
run-name: "build-macos (create_release=${{ inputs.create_release }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.0.2) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      create_release:
        description: 'Create GitHub Release'
        required: false
        default: 'true'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'true'
          - 'false'

# Release builds are never preempted (issue #194 pt 5, same principle as
# ci.yml: tag/release runs must not be cancelled mid-flight; gh-1537
# retired the post-merge main ci run).
concurrency:
  group: Build macOS Release (Fa)-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — release-attaching jobs grant
# contents: write in their own job-level blocks.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-macos:
    name: Build macOS ${{ matrix.arch }}
    needs: version
    # gh-1600 F-A: pin the ONE self-hosted macOS runner (fa-m5-1) via its
    # unique registration label — the generic [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
    # list also matched the Linux self-hosted box's labels (same routing
    # bug that sent the build-mobile iOS jobs to Linux, gh-1600).
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    # Issue #239: TestFlight submit now waits for Apple processing (bounded,
    # default 90 min) + a ~1-min one-shot appearance probe AFTER the
    # build/notarize work (gh-1041: the blocking distribution wait moved to
    # the deferred store-appearance-check workflow) — the job ceiling must
    # cover the worst case, not just the build.
    timeout-minutes: 150
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        arch: [arm64, x86_64]
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # Workaround: force .NET (used by the runner) to use SocketsHttpHandler
      # instead of Apple's SSL APIs, avoiding "bad certificate format" errors
      # caused by corporate Zscaler/MDM certificates in the system keychain.
      DOTNET_SYSTEM_NET_HTTP_USESOCKETSHTTPHANDLER: "0"
      # gh-1814: these release legs ride the Swift Package Manager lane.
      # History: gh-180 pinned the legs to PURE CocoaPods via the job-level
      # FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=0 override because Flutter 3.47's
      # best-effort, silent FlutterGeneratedPluginSwiftPackage floor bump
      # (xcodebuild -showBuildSettings inside updateMinimumDeployment)
      # skipped on the first Xcode 27 run (run 39905803673, "requires
      # minimum platform version 14.0" → no DMGs in v1.0.630). That pin is
      # GONE now: upstream removed the disable knob between 3.47.4 and
      # 3.47.7 (flutter/flutter#193978 — the day the gh-180 shelf-life
      # comment predicted), and the pinned-3.47.7 legs added SwiftPM
      # integration anyway (runs 39991663029 / 40022900373), reding the
      # gh-180 gate that forbade SwiftPM state. The #1813 escape (pin
      # 3.47.4) is operationally dead — the runners cannot fetch that SDK
      # (run 40034163885). Owner ruling: the minimum macOS version may be
      # raised, so the lane ADOPTS SwiftPM instead of fighting it:
      #   - every floor is ≥ 14.0 and stays there — Runner pbxproj 3×14.0,
      #     Podfile platform :osx, '14.0' (the CocoaPods half: the vendored
      #     flutter_inappwebview_macos keeps its Package.swift deleted,
      #     gh-1798, riding Podfile.lock pins), generated package floor
      #     bumped to the app's MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET by the tool
      #     (verified working on 3.47.7: gate diagnostic
      #     `generated floor: 14.0`);
      #   - scripts/assert_macos_min_platform.sh (the Build macOS release
      #     step below) ASSERTS the SPM lane post-config — SwiftPM state
      #     EXPECTED, generated floor ≥ app floor, no product above the app
      #     min — still fail-loud-in-seconds.
      # Pinned by test/build_macos_spm_lane_guard_test.dart +
      # test/macos_min_platform_gate_test.dart.

    steps:
      # ── Prepare persistent local git mirrors ────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1644: the old inline single-shot logic died on the first network
      # hiccup — the recreate fell through to a full `git clone --mirror`
      # whose ~1 h transfer ended in "error: 2931 bytes of body are still
      # expected" (run 38855793382, exit 128). The shared script retries the
      # fetch with VISIBLE stderr, aborts stalled attempts, and recreates
      # BLOBLESS (--filter=blob:none, the gh-1477 precedent) with retries and
      # partial-dir cleanup. Contract: scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
      # gh-1665 review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent
      # self-hosted runners — the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree (or be
      # wiped), so the script is bootstrapped from the commit-pinned raw URL
      # (workflow_dispatch-only workflows ⇒ ${{ github.sha }} is always a
      # pushed commit) with the mirror copy as the no-network fallback.
      - name: Update local git mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          mkdir -p "$MIRROR_BASE"
          MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — syncing the mirror and falling back to its copy" >&2
            # gh-1665 review (returned IMPORTANT): in the one-run-wide
            # first-post-merge window the persistent mirror is still a
            # PRE-MERGE tree. Cheap single-shot ensure (bounded resilience
            # stays owned by $SCRIPT below) so the extraction that follows
            # succeeds on any runner that can reach github.com at all —
            # raw.githubusercontent.com being down degrades to the
            # fallback instead of a red leg.
            if [ -d "$MIRROR" ] && git -C "$MIRROR" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin || true
            else
              rm -rf "$MIRROR"
              git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR" || true
            fi
            BRANCH="$(git --git-dir="$MIRROR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
            git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" > "$SCRIPT" \
              || { echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (raw URL unreachable and mirror lacks the script)" >&2; exit 1; }
          fi
          bash "$SCRIPT" \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git \
            "$MIRROR"

      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout — the bare `rm -rf
      # "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` used to fail the whole checkout on stale
      # unremovable leftovers in the persistent shared workspace (bench
      # docker leftovers, jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/). Log-and-prune clean +
      # clone-around-stub; the per-arch build cache is parked outside the
      # workspace before the clean and restored after the clone (best-effort:
      # a lost cache re-builds from scratch, it never fails the checkout).
      # INLINE (not a composite action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...`
      # actions resolve against $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box
      # that is the PREVIOUS run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/" \
              || echo "::warning::could not park the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

          cd /tmp

          # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
          # shared workspace — log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf build/macos 2>/dev/null || true
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/ \
              || echo "::warning::could not restore the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): same rationale as
      # build-mobile.yml — on a persistent self-hosted runner the
      # flutter-action cache costs a ~1GB untar on setup plus a whole-SDK
      # re-tar POST per job. The composite action pins the SDK at
      # ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk (.fah-version marker):
      # subsecond reuse, one download per pin bump, no POST step.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install instead of the runner's
      # pre-installed SDK — the candidate-path loop picked up a stale
      # 3.44.4 at ~/.local/flutter, which broke `flutter pub get` the
      # moment the repo floor moved to >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260/#261).
      - name: Setup Flutter environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          # EXACT patch pin (#1431): this leg builds + gates fa-extension.zip
          # against scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv — a wildcard pin
          # re-resolves a new engine build on every 3.47.x patch and moves
          # the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the gate tracks. Bump
          # consciously, with any floor reseed in the same PR.
          #
          # 3.47.7 (gh-1814, reverting the #1813 3.47.4 pin): 3.47.4 was
          # the last patch honoring FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=0, but it
          # is UNREACHABLE here — the fa-m5 runners' ~60kB/s link cannot
          # download that SDK (run 40034163885 died in the download, bounded
          # retries exhausted) — and with the SPM lane adopted (see the job
          # env comment above) there is no reason to chase it: 3.47.7's
          # forced SPM integration is now the lane, its floor bump verified
          # working (`generated floor: 14.0` in the run 40022900373 gate
          # diagnostic), and scripts/assert_macos_min_platform.sh asserts
          # the post-config state. Same 3.47.7 the extension + Pages legs
          # already pin.
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'

      - name: Setup host toolchains
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          flutter --version
          dart --version

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: |
          if command -v rustup &> /dev/null; then
            echo "Rust already installed"
            rustup show
          else
            echo "Installing Rust..."
            curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y
            source "$HOME/.cargo/env"
          fi
          echo "$HOME/.cargo/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          rustup --version
          cargo --version

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The plist is gitignored, so the fresh CI checkout has none and the
      # native Firebase SDK logs I-COR000012/0008 at startup. Inject it from
      # a secret when available (same dev.fa1.app registration as
      # firebase_options.dart).
      - name: Write GoogleService-Info.plist (macOS)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/macos/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist
            echo "GoogleService-Info.plist written (bundle: $(plutil -extract BUNDLE_ID raw flutter_app/macos/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64 not set — building without the native Firebase plist"
          fi

      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Dependency versions
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          echo "=== Dependency versions ==="
          flutter pub deps --style=compact

      # flutter_gemma ≥1.5.5 no longer downloads the Apple LiteRT-LM companion
      # dylibs from its hook (they are bundled via the Podfile phase), so a
      # fresh runner has nothing at ~/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma and the
      # Runner script phase fails with "Could not find macOS companion
      # dylibs". Seed the cache from the upstream native release (pinned,
      # sha256-verified).
      - name: Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion dylibs
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma/native/macos_arm64"
          if [ -f "$GEMMA_CACHE/libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib" ]; then
            echo "companion dylibs already cached"
          else
            echo "seeding companion dylibs from flutter_gemma native-v0.16.0"
            mkdir -p "$GEMMA_CACHE"
            # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56);
            # --retry-all-errors retries them (sha256 below guards corruption)
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
              -o /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz \
              https://github.com/DenisovAV/flutter_gemma/releases/download/native-v0.16.0/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz
            echo "c597554a7a5cdf099658227099a54ef4916c5802b9182757e656e1788f9426b6  /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz" | shasum -a 256 -c -
            tar xzf /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz -C "$GEMMA_CACHE"
          fi
          ls -la "$GEMMA_CACHE"

      # The workspace is re-cloned every run, which wipes Pods/ and forces a
      # full pod install (~4 min with Firebase). Cache it keyed by the
      # lockfile; $HOME-level caches (pub-cache, CocoaPods download cache,
      # Ruby gems, Flutter SDK) already persist on the self-hosted runner.
      - name: Cache CocoaPods (macOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: flutter_app/macos/Pods
          key: macos-pods-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/macos/Podfile.lock') }}

      - name: Generate build info
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
          GIT_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
          SUBMODULES=$(git submodule status --recursive | tr '\n' ';')

          mkdir -p lib/core/services
          printf '%s\n' \
            '// Generated build info — CI overwrites this file before compilation.' \
            '// ignore_for_file: constant_identifier_names' \
            '' \
            "const String kBuildGitCommit = '${GIT_COMMIT}';" \
            "const String kBuildGitBranch = '${GIT_BRANCH}';" \
            "const String kBuildSubmodules = '${SUBMODULES}';" \
            > lib/core/services/build_info.dart

          echo "Build info generated:"
          cat lib/core/services/build_info.dart

      - name: Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework
          key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 20
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (keyed by the release tag) — warm until the
          #    repo's daily cache churn LRU-evicts the entry (saved 10-20
          #    06:02Z, gone by 10-21 19:03Z: gh-1759 ran cold twice);
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the step
          #    cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): retries live in THIS
          #    bash loop, not curl --retry (which adds N MORE attempts AND
          #    restarts+truncates instead of resuming). Worst case with the
          #    gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s,
          #    + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (1200s) cap.
          #
          #    gh-1759: the gh-1149 budget (3 × 240s) was sized for this
          #    link's good-day ~300KB/s. The 10-21 daily run measured
          #    40–108KB/s (cold cache, both arch jobs): 3 × 240s banked
          #    only 29.5MB (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) of the 97,238,501-byte
          #    asset and the leg went red. Resume worked (`Resuming
          #    transfer from byte position …` in the logs) — the wire
          #    budget was simply too small, and the old pre-loop wipe
          #    threw each run's partial away, so a slow-link day never
          #    banked durable progress and the leg could not self-heal.
          #    Fixes: (a) the per-arch /tmp partial now PERSISTS across
          #    runs — -C - resumes it within the step AND across daily
          #    runs (macOS prunes only 3-day-untouched /tmp files; a daily
          #    run touches it) until the asset completes and the
          #    actions/cache post-step saves the framework; (b) the loop
          #    grew to 4 × 240s under a 20-min step cap.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
          # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
          # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
          # let one job's cleanup unlink the other's in-flight partial,
          # then both curls interleave bytes into one path.
          ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
          # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
          # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
          # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern
          # as the litertlm download above). The pinned byte size tells a
          # truncated download (KEEP the partial — the next run resumes
          # it) apart from a complete-but-wrong one (PURGE and restart).
          ASSET_DIGEST="aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"
          ASSET_BYTES=97238501
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # The partial is deliberately NOT deleted between runs
            # (gh-1759): it is exactly what -C - is for. If the persisted
            # zip is already complete AND digest-valid, skip the download
            # — a -C - attempt against a complete file gets HTTP 416 and
            # reads success as failure.
            if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
            else
              for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
                # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
                # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
                # engages this loop's retries. -C - makes each attempt
                # RESUME the partial zip (Range requests), so slow links
                # make forward progress within this step AND across runs.
                if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                  -o "$ZIP" \
                  https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                  break
                fi
                if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
                else
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
                  sleep 5
                fi
              done
              got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)
              if [ "$got" -eq "$ASSET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
                : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
              elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASSET_BYTES" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASSET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2
                exit 1
              else
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip is $got bytes (expected $ASSET_BYTES) or failed its pinned sha256 — purging it so the next run restarts clean" >&2
                rm -f "$ZIP"
                exit 1
              fi
            fi
            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # Per-arch keychain: both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted
      # runner; a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create
      # emptied it under the other's codesign — errSecInternalComponent /
      # "No certificate found", builds 86).
      - name: Import macOS signing certificate
        id: signing
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "⚠️  No signing certificate found — building unsigned (development only)"
            echo "signed=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "✅ Signing certificate found — importing..."
            security delete-keychain build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain 2>/dev/null || true
            security create-keychain -p "$MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security default-keychain -s build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security unlock-keychain -p "$MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            # gh-1798: the window must cover the WHOLE job, not the
            # import→build gap. On the first Xcode 27 run the tool's
            # "Adding Swift Package Manager integration" pass alone took
            # 3365s (56 min) + 443s pod install, putting the first codesign
            # evaluation 73+ min after unlock — the 1h window auto-locked
            # the keychain mid-build and codesign lost the identity
            # ("No certificate for team ... matching ... found"). 4h ≥ the
            # 150-min job ceiling with slack. Pinned by
            # test/ci_macos_signing_window_guard_test.dart.
            security set-keychain-settings -t 14400 -u build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            security list-keychains -d user -s build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db

            echo "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64" | base64 --decode > certificate.p12
            security import certificate.p12 -k build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain \
              -P "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD" \
              -T /usr/bin/codesign \
              -T /usr/bin/productbuild
            security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k "$MACOS_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" build-${{ matrix.arch }}.keychain
            echo "signed=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

          if [ -n "$MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode > profile.provisionprofile
            echo "profile_embedded=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

            # Make the profile visible to Xcode manual signing.
            PROFILE_UUID=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract UUID raw -)
            PROFILE_NAME=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Name raw -)
            PROFILE_TEAM=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract TeamIdentifier.0 raw - 2>/dev/null || true)
            echo "Profile: $PROFILE_NAME / UUID: $PROFILE_UUID / team: $PROFILE_TEAM"
            mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles"
            cp profile.provisionprofile "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles/${PROFILE_UUID}.provisionprofile"
            echo "profile_uuid=$PROFILE_UUID" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "profile_team=$PROFILE_TEAM" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "⚠️  No provisioning profile found — TestFlight will warn"
            echo "profile_embedded=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Build macOS release (${{ matrix.arch }})
        env:
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          BUILD_VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID }}
          PROFILE_UUID: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_uuid }}
          PROFILE_TEAM: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_team }}
        run: |
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          echo "Building for architecture: $ARCH"
          cd flutter_app
          if [ -n "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID:-}" ]; then
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID"
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual
            if [ -n "${MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID:-}" ]; then
              export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID"
            elif [ -n "${PROFILE_TEAM:-}" ]; then
              export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$PROFILE_TEAM"
            fi
            if [ -n "${PROFILE_UUID:-}" ]; then
              export FA_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER="$PROFILE_UUID"
            fi
          else
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-"
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic
          fi
          # gh-1814 REG gate — fail loud at build time, not at release time.
          # --config-only drives the tool's real SPM/pods config pass
          # (the SwiftPM migration + pod install) without compiling; the
          # gate then ASSERTS the adopted SPM lane: SwiftPM state EXPECTED
          # after the config pass (pbxproj marker + ephemeral generated
          # package), app floor 14.0 (pbxproj + Podfile), generated package
          # floor ≥ 14.0 (the tool's silent showBuildSettings bump must
          # have landed — the literal gh-180 killer), no SwiftPM product
          # above the app min, and the vendored inappwebview manifest
          # floored at 14.0 if it ever reappears. A drift fails in seconds
          # with the remediation instead of Xcode's cryptic "requires
          # minimum platform version" error after a 50+-minute resolution
          # pass (gh-1798 measured 3365s on the first Xcode 27 run).
          # gh-1800 follow-up (the residue clean stays): self-hosted
          # workdirs are PERSISTENT — untracked build state (macos/Flutter/
          # ephemeral, Pods, .symlinks) survives actions/checkout, so it is
          # wiped before every build and the config-only pass regenerates a
          # DETERMINISTIC fresh SPM migration + pod install (the pre-#1812
          # runs showed stale residue steering the lane). The gate below
          # then sees exactly the state a fresh 3.47.7 config pass
          # produces.
          flutter clean
          rm -rf macos/Flutter/ephemeral macos/Pods macos/.symlinks
          FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS="$ARCH" flutter build macos --config-only
          bash ../scripts/assert_macos_min_platform.sh 14.0
          FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS="$ARCH" flutter build macos --release \
            --build-name=$BUILD_VERSION \
            --build-number=$BUILD_NUMBER
          MAIN_BIN=$(find build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app -name "Fa" -type f | head -1)
          echo "=== Binary architecture verification ==="
          echo "Binary path: $MAIN_BIN"
          file "$MAIN_BIN"
          lipo -info "$MAIN_BIN"
          echo "=== End binary verification ==="
          # The Dart side resolves the wasm_run FFI surface via dlsym on the
          # main executable. If the symbols were dead-stripped or not exported
          # the app boots to a white screen on TestFlight — fail here instead.
          echo "=== wasm_run FFI symbol verification ==="
          # dyld_info reads the exports trie, which survives stripping
          # (nm -gD fails on stripped binaries with "no dynamic symbol table").
          EXPORTS=$(xcrun dyld_info -exports "$MAIN_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true)
          WIRE_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " _wire_" || true)
          echo "wasm_run wire_* exports in binary: $WIRE_COUNT"
          for SYM in _wire_compile_wasm _store_dart_post_cobject _init_frb_dart_api_dl; do
            if ! echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -qE " ${SYM}\$"; then
              echo "::error::$SYM is not exported from the app binary — wasm_run would crash at runtime (white screen)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "✅ wasm_run FFI symbols are exported"

      - name: Package as DMG
        id: package
        env:
          SIGNED: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.signed }}
          PROFILE_EMBEDDED: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_embedded }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          APP_PATH="flutter_app/build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app"
          DMG_NAME="fa-macos-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.dmg"

          # Size diet (#1096 AC4 + direction 3): drop what no macOS code path
          # can load — before any codesign so the seal covers the shipped
          # tree. Both cuts ride in flutter_assets inside App.framework:
          # 1) assets/wasm (~47 MB) — WASI interpreter modules loaded
          #    exclusively via WasiSandboxShell (env_factory_io.dart routes
          #    desktops to the host Process shell; every rootBundle.load of
          #    assets/wasm lives in the mobile-only shell).
          # 2) packages/js_widget_runtime/test — the pub package's
          #    own test fixture (coach_anny.glb, 5.6 MB); nothing in the app
          #    references that path (the live model, when used, is fetched
          #    by the JS-app catalog, not bundled).
          ASSETS="$APP_PATH/Contents/Frameworks/App.framework/Versions/A/Resources/flutter_assets"
          # Shared prune (scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh — the same call
          # runs on the no-sandbox build and every web packaging surface):
          # fails loudly if the flutter_assets layout drifts instead of
          # silently shipping the fat bundle. Re-enable path (review,
          # #1096): if a desktop WASI/sandbox mode ever ships
          # (WasiSandboxShell on macOS), reseed assets/wasm — until then a
          # desktop wasm load would fail as a missing asset, not a
          # #1224-class "no lazy loader" stub.
          bash scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh "$ASSETS" \
            assets/wasm packages/js_widget_runtime/test

          rm -f fa-macos-*.dmg tmp-fa.dmg
          rm -rf dmg-staging

          echo "Packaging: $APP_PATH → $DMG_NAME (arch: $ARCH)"

          if [ "$SIGNED" = "true" ] && [ -n "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" ]; then
            echo "Signing .app bundle..."

            RESVG_BIN="$APP_PATH/Contents/Resources/resvg"
            if [ -f "$RESVG_BIN" ]; then
              echo "Stripping extended attributes from resvg..."
              xattr -cr "$RESVG_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true
              echo "Signing resvg binary..."
              codesign --force --sign "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                "$RESVG_BIN"
            fi

            find "$APP_PATH" -type f \( -perm +111 -o -name '*.dylib' \) | while read -r bin; do
              if codesign -dv "$bin" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID"; then
                continue
              fi
              echo "Signing nested binary: $bin"
              codesign --force --sign "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                "$bin" 2>/dev/null || true
            done

            if [ "$PROFILE_EMBEDDED" = "true" ] && [ -f "profile.provisionprofile" ]; then
              echo "Embedding provisioning profile..."
              cp profile.provisionprofile "$APP_PATH/Contents/embedded.provisionprofile"
              APP_ID=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Entitlements xml1 -o - - | grep -A 1 'com.apple.application-identifier' | tail -1 | sed 's/.*<string>\(.*\)<\/string>.*/\1/')
              TEAM_ID="${APP_ID%%.*}"
              # Start from Release.entitlements (network client+server, file
              # bookmarks, calendar, contacts, health, homekit, audio input)
              # and inject the provisioning identity keys — do NOT collapse
              # to a sandbox-only dict: the app needs every entitlement the
              # sandbox declares, and dropping them breaks SSO callback
              # servers, file access, and OS-level permission flows in the
              # signed production build.
              cp flutter_app/macos/Runner/Release.entitlements entitlements.plist
              # PlistBuddy handles dotted top-level key names (plutil
              # -insert/-replace treats dots as nested key separators).
              /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Add :com.apple.application-identifier string $APP_ID" entitlements.plist
              /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Add :com.apple.developer.team-identifier string $TEAM_ID" entitlements.plist
              # The profile may not grant every *capability* the app declares
              # (e.g. homekit needs a separate App ID capability in the
              # Developer Portal). TestFlight rejects capability entitlements
              # the profile doesn't include ('Invalid Code Signing
              # Entitlements', error 90285).
              #
              # Only com.apple.developer.* keys are profile-gated. The
              # com.apple.security.* sandbox entitlements (network, files,
              # personal-information) are NOT in the profile by design — any
              # sandboxed app may declare them — so they must survive.
              #
              # NOTE: `plutil -extract ... -o -` (stdout form) is not
              # supported on every macOS the runner may have; use real temp
              # files so the extraction can't silently produce nothing.
              security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile -o profile_decoded.plist
              plutil -extract Entitlements json profile_decoded.plist -o profile_ents.json
              for KEY in $(plutil -convert xml1 entitlements.plist -o - | grep -o '<key>[^<]*</key>' | sed 's/<[^>]*>//g'); do
                case "$KEY" in
                  com.apple.application-identifier|com.apple.developer.team-identifier) continue ;;
                  com.apple.developer.*) ;;
                  *) continue ;; # sandbox + misc entitlements are not profile-gated
                esac
                if ! python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('profile_ents.json')); raise SystemExit(0 if '$KEY' in d else 1)"; then
                  echo "Dropping capability not granted by profile: $KEY"
                  /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Delete :$KEY" entitlements.plist
                fi
              done
              ENTITLEMENTS="entitlements.plist"
            else
              ENTITLEMENTS="flutter_app/macos/Runner/Release.entitlements"
            fi

            codesign_app() {
              codesign --force --deep --sign "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" \
                "$APP_PATH"
            }

            for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
              if codesign_app; then
                break
              fi
              if [ "$attempt" = "5" ]; then
                echo "codesign failed after $attempt attempts"
                exit 1
              fi
              sleep_seconds=$((attempt * 30))
              echo "codesign failed, retrying in ${sleep_seconds}s (attempt $attempt/5)..."
              sleep "$sleep_seconds"
            done

            echo "Verifying code signature..."
            codesign -vv --deep --strict "$APP_PATH"
            spctl -a -vv "$APP_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi

          DMG_STAGING="dmg-staging"
          rm -rf "$DMG_STAGING"
          mkdir "$DMG_STAGING"
          cp -R "$APP_PATH" "$DMG_STAGING/"
          ln -s /Applications "$DMG_STAGING/Applications"

          TMP_DMG="tmp-fa.dmg"
          hdiutil create \
            -volname "Fa $VERSION" \
            -srcfolder "$DMG_STAGING" \
            -ov \
            -format UDRW \
            "$TMP_DMG"

          hdiutil convert "$TMP_DMG" -format UDZO -o "$DMG_NAME"
          rm -f "$TMP_DMG"
          rm -rf "$DMG_STAGING"

          echo "dmg_name=$DMG_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          ZIP_NAME="fa-macos-${ARCH}-${VERSION}-mac.zip"
          echo "Packaging ZIP for auto-update: $ZIP_NAME"
          ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent "$APP_PATH" "$ZIP_NAME"
          SHA512=$(openssl dgst -sha512 -binary "$ZIP_NAME" | openssl base64 -A)
          SIZE=$(stat -f%z "$ZIP_NAME")
          MANIFEST_ARCH="$ARCH"
          if [ "$MANIFEST_ARCH" = "x86_64" ]; then
            MANIFEST_ARCH="x64"
          fi
          MANIFEST_NAME="latest-mac-${MANIFEST_ARCH}.yml"
          RELEASE_DATE=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z")
          printf '%s\n' \
            "version: ${VERSION}" \
            "files:" \
            "  - url: ${ZIP_NAME}" \
            "    sha512: ${SHA512}" \
            "    size: ${SIZE}" \
            "    arch: ${MANIFEST_ARCH}" \
            "path: ${ZIP_NAME}" \
            "sha512: ${SHA512}" \
            "releaseDate: '${RELEASE_DATE}'" \
            > "$MANIFEST_NAME"
          echo "zip_name=$ZIP_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "manifest_name=$MANIFEST_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "baseline_arch=$MANIFEST_ARCH" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      # AC1 (#1096): per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget gate on
      # the shipped mac zip (auto-update channel). arm64 baseline is
      # committed, reseeded onto the post-cut shape (#1096 size diet: no
      # wasm_run_flutter.framework, no flutter_assets/assets/wasm, no
      # js_widget_runtime test assets — regrowth of any of those fails as

    name: Build macOS CLI ${{ matrix.arch }}
    needs: version
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351): dart
    # CLI bundle + release upload; the two arches run in PARALLEL on
    # GitHub-hosted runners (they do not serialize like the self-hosted
    # build-macos matrix does).
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: macos-latest
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            arch: x64
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh — same
          # reason as release-macos's checkout (gh-1477: the notes read
          # commit MESSAGES, never historical file blobs).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        run: |
          version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary
        run: |
          codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Archive and upload CLI bundle
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          # Matrix legs share GITHUB_JOB=build-macos-cli — the leg-suffixed
          # draft owner identity keeps the guard below scoped to the leg
          # that created the draft, never the sibling's mid-upload one.
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-macos-${{ matrix.arch }}.tar.gz"
          tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          ls -lh "$asset"

          # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first, publish is PROVENANCE-OWNED.
          # The CLI tarball is a `fa update` asset, but servability needs
          # the SIGNED SHA256SUMS — which only the tag-run's
          # release-provenance job uploads (ci.yml). So: create the draft
          # lazily (curated notes via release_notes.sh + THIS leg's
          # draft-owner marker the guard below can reclaim), upload, and
          # let provenance own the --draft=false --latest flip.
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"
          gh release upload "$RELEASE_TAG" "$asset" --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): this job creates releases,
      # so a failed/cancelled run must not leave one behind as a draft.
      # Leg-scoped (gh-1801): matches only THIS arch leg's marker.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: size-baselines-web-spa
          path: scripts/size_budget/*.tsv
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload bundle to GitHub Release
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first and NEVER publish here. The web
          # zip is not a `fa update` asset — and even a CLI asset alone
          # would not make the release servable: the SIGNED SHA256SUMS
          # only lands in release-provenance, which owns the
          # --draft=false --latest flip. Create/attach the draft with the
          # curated notes + a draft-owner marker (guard/sweeper-visible)
          # and upload.
          # No guard step here ON PURPOSE: this job is continue-on-error —
          # on failure the train (binaries → provenance) CONTINUES and
          # must find the draft alive; a genuinely orphaned draft is
          # reclaimed by the 24h sweeper (GITHUB_TOKEN-authored → bot).
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" fa-web-spa.zip --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # continue-on-error keeps the job/check green even on failure — a
      # release can then only be gated on a MISSING asset. Surface the miss
      # in the run's step summary too (covers upload flakes, not just guard
      # trips); the failed steps remain visible in the job view.
      - name: Flag missing bundle in step summary
        if: failure()
        run: |
          {
            echo '## fa-web-spa.zip NOT shipped this release'
            echo ''
            echo 'The web SPA bundle job failed (continue-on-error: the release ships without it). See the failed steps above.'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # SEC-07 (#795): the installer's default trust path is SIGNED checksums.
  # This job aggregates every fa-* asset of the release into SHA256SUMS and
  # signs it with the FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY repo secret (openssl RSA —
  # already available on runners, no new dependency). The signing key is a
  # channel separate from the release assets, so a checksum file served from
  # the same compromised source as the binary cannot vouch for itself.
  # Fail-closed: without the secret the release publishes NO provenance and
  # this job goes red — install.sh aborts with E_PROVENANCE_MISSING on it.
  # Needs web-spa (#1100, continue-on-error) for ordering only: the web
  # bundle cannot hold CLI provenance hostage. The ordering makes the fa-*
  # sweep deterministic — web-spa success -> zip signed, web-spa failure ->
  # zip absent — never a half-updated manifest.
  release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —
          # the first moment `fa update` can actually serve it (it
          # hard-fails without the signed checksums, bin/self_manage.dart).
          # Flip draft=false + latest here and ONLY here: a red provenance
          # leaves the previous release as latest (safe degradation)
          # instead of stranding a provenance-less one (the v1.0.630
          # empty/partial-latest window class).
          gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

  # gh-1832 AC3: post-publish smoke. Probes (1) EVERY releases/(latest/)?
  # download/ URL the fa1.dev landing page exposes (site/index.html) and
  # (2) the full required set from scripts/release_required_assets.txt via
  # a 1-byte ranged GET each — red on anything but HTTP 200/206. Rides the
  # tag train only (PR runs never probe release URLs); a 404 here is the
  # owner-facing v1.0.635 symptom caught the same hour it appears.
  release-asset-smoke:
    name: Release asset smoke (landing links + required set)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.release-provenance.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Probe every landing-page release link
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --landing site/index.html
      - name: Probe the full required asset set
        env:
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --smoke "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun
    # went green, the marker never advanced). With always() the job RUNS
    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Point the vpinned marker at ${{ github.ref_name }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/pin_release.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

  installer-smoke:
    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Depends on binaries — no !cancelled() needed here: the skip chain is
    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            kind: ps1
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            kind: sh

# gh-1832: the REQUIRED release-asset set — the single source of truth.
#
# Consumers (all read this one file, never a private copy):
#   - ci.yml release-provenance "Assert required release assets" step —
#     the publish-blocking gate: runs scripts/assert_release_assets.sh
#     <tag> BEFORE the signed-checksums upload and the --draft=false
#     --latest flip. A missing asset leaves the release a DRAFT (the
#     previous release stays latest) and fails the release run loudly.
#   - ci.yml release-asset-smoke job — post-publish: --smoke ranged-GETs
#     every asset here (red on non-200/206) and --landing probes every
#     releases/(latest/)?download/ URL the fa1.dev landing page exposes.
#
# Scope: exactly the fa-* set a usable release must serve (v1.0.634 is the
# reference shape — v1.0.635 shipped without fa-extension.zip, gh-1832):
# `fa update` channels (linux/macos/windows archives), the web SPA and the
# Chrome extension the landing page links directly.
#
# Deliberately NOT here: SHA256SUMS(.sig) — release-provenance itself
# produces them after this gate runs; DMGs/zips/latest-mac.yml and the
# store artifacts (apk/aab/ipa) — they come from the separately-dispatched
# daily mobile/macOS legs (a flaky self-hosted runner must never hold the
# CLI/web/extension train hostage) and are clobber-refresher assets, not
# publish blockers.
#
# One literal asset name per line; '#' starts a comment. The gate matches
# exact names — no globs.
fa-extension.zip
fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz
fa-linux-x64.tar.gz
fa-macos-arm64.tar.gz
fa-macos-x64.tar.gz
fa-web-spa.zip
fa-windows-x64.zip
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-1832: release required-assets gate + post-publish smoke.
#
# The single source of truth for the required set is the file next to this
# script: scripts/release_required_assets.txt (scope rationale lives in its
# header). Three modes:
#
#   assert_release_assets.sh <tag>
#       PUBLISH GATE (ci.yml release-provenance, before the signed-checksum
#       upload and the --draft=false --latest flip): every required asset
#       name must already be attached to <tag>'s release (draft counts).
#       Anything missing → ::error:: + exit 1 → the release run goes red
#       and the release stays a draft (the previous release stays latest).
#       This is the rehearsal-proven guard for the v1.0.635 incident, where
#       the extension's producer (build-macos.yml build-extension, a daily
#       leg that derives "latest+1 at its own dispatch moment") attached
#       fa-extension.zip to an orphaned v1.0.636 draft while the tag train
#       published v1.0.635 without it — every leg green, nothing asserted
#       the published set.
#
#   assert_release_assets.sh --smoke <tag|latest>
#       POST-PUBLISH SMOKE: ranged-GET (1 byte) every required asset's
#       download URL; anything outside HTTP 200/206 fails. Base URL is
#       https://github.com unless FA_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE overrides it
#       (tests), repo comes from GITHUB_REPOSITORY.
#
#   assert_release_assets.sh --landing [page]
#       LANDING LINK-CHECK: extracts EVERY http(s) …/releases/(latest/)?
#       download/… URL from the landing page (default site/index.html) and
#       probes each the same way — the page's links can never silently rot
#       again (the owner-facing symptom of gh-1832 was exactly this 404).
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN (gate mode), FA_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE
# (smoke/landing override, tests only).
set -euo pipefail

script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
required_file="$script_dir/release_required_assets.txt"
[ -s "$required_file" ] || {
  echo "::error::required-assets list $required_file is missing/empty — refusing to judge a release against an empty set" >&2
  exit 1
}
# The list, comments stripped, order kept.
required=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
  line="${line%%#*}"
  line="$(printf '%s' "$line" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  [ -n "$line" ] && required+=("$line")
done < "$required_file"
[ "${#required[@]}" -gt 0 ] || {
  echo "::error::$required_file parsed to zero assets — fix the list" >&2
  exit 1
}

# One ranged GET; prints the HTTP code. 200/206 = served (206 = the
# Range: bytes=0-0 answer of a real CDN download, i.e. an actual
# 1-byte download probe, not a name check).
probe_url() {
  local url="$1" code
  code=$(curl -sS -L --range 0-0 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
    --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 60 "$url" 2>/dev/null) || true
  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
  # Always emit the code (the caller's success line shows it); the
  # function's exit status carries the verdict.
  echo "$code"
  case "$code" in
    200|206) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

mode="${1:?usage: assert_release_assets.sh <tag> | --smoke <tag|latest> | --landing [page]}"

case "$mode" in
  --smoke)
    tag="${2:?usage: assert_release_assets.sh --smoke <tag|latest>}"
    repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
    base="${FA_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE:-https://github.com}"
    fail=0
    for asset in "${required[@]}"; do
      if [ "$tag" = "latest" ]; then
        url="$base/$repo/releases/latest/download/$asset"
      else
        url="$base/$repo/releases/download/$tag/$asset"
      fi
      if ! code="$(probe_url "$url")"; then
        echo "::error::release asset smoke FAILED: $url → HTTP $code (gh-1832: a required asset does not serve)" >&2

Release-train recovery playbook (gh-1845, 2026-10-24): when a v* tag run's "Sign release checksums" (release-provenance) fails with "release <tag> is missing 1 required asset(s): fa-extension.zip — BLOCKING the publish", the fix is NOT code: dispatch the producer with an explicit tag — `gh workflow run build-macos.yml --ref <tag> -f version=<tag> -f create_release=true` (its build-extension job is ubuntu-latest, fast, and adopts the existing draft via scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh) — wait for fa-extension.zip to appear on the release, then `gh run rerun <tag-run-id> --failed`. Root pattern: build-macos.yml build-extension derives "latest+1 at its own dispatch moment" and runs ~once daily, so any tag train landing after the daily leg has no fa-extension.zip and the gh-1832 gate correctly strands it as a draft (seen stuck: v1.0.637, v1.0.638 on 2026-10-24). Also: a rerun --failed never resurrects SKIPPED jobs (e.g. Installer smoke) — benign, the Quality gate treats skipped as neutral. Systemic fix tracked as follow-up gh-1847 (tag train producing/attaching fa-extension.zip itself, or an event-driven producer) so this manual dispatch stays an emergency procedure, not the operating mode.

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the quality gate is NOT re-run by
  # the release twin — the release-dedupe pre-check (gh-1625) short-circuits
  # every gate leg when the tag's GREEN push run already gates it, while
  # the release-specific legs (binaries attach, release-provenance,
  # installer-smoke) keep running on the twin (the retired comment here
  # only made the binaries UPLOAD idempotent — duplicate create +
  # --clobber, last wins — while the full 35-40 min gate still re-ran,
  # doubling release wall time).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage

#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet

#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)

web-spa:
    name: Build web SPA bundle
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Additive asset: a web-build failure (guard trip, SDK flake) must NOT
    # hold the release hostage — CLI provenance (SHA256SUMS) and the vpinned
    # bump still ship. Job-level continue-on-error reports the job (and its
    # check) as SUCCESS — the failed steps stay visible on the run page for
    # the manual check. Downstream needs see success; the provenance fa-*
    # sweep then deterministically finds no zip (success -> signed,
    # failure -> absent — never a half-updated manifest).
    continue-on-error: true
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach fa-web-spa.zip to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh — same
          # reason as the binaries job's checkout above.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      # Same pinned SDK as build-web / the release path (#281); EXACT patch
      # pin (#1431): a wildcard re-resolves a new engine build on every
      # 3.47.x patch and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the size

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file"' EXIT
if ! bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes.sh" "$tag" >"$notes_file" ||
  [ ! -s "$notes_file" ]; then
  printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" >"$notes_file"
fi
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"

# DRAFT-first (gh-1801): a create here must never publish — the resolved
# asset list at this point can never include the signed checksums. The
# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release).
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || true
echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
